review.source: history://Kiln45Review on the #45 slice as integrated in 4ccae671; decisions by Main

findings.summary: Recovery could settle an executed attempt after the profile's Lattice state root changed, because recover used the current profile's root.
findings.resolution: Before the first run's transport intent, worker::run creates the state root and retains OUTPUT/transport-binding-ATTEMPT-FENCE.json (kiln.lattice-transport-binding.v1; exclusive create, 0400, file and directory fsync, byte equality on conflict) with the program, its BLAKE3 and the root. recover uses only the bound values, re-hashes the bound program, and without a binding or with a bound root that is not a directory refuses before invoking Lattice. A closure settles only from a bound recover.

findings.summary: stale_fence with dispatched:false is not a durable no-start proof: Lattice db64cd65 checks the fence (session/fencing.rs:81-101) before writing the intent (cli/execution.rs:169-240).
findings.resolution: stale_fence is no longer settled, and every refusal returned by recover is retained; only run refusals of crossed_attempt, profile_revision_superseded, revision_not_admitted and revision_blocked with dispatched:false settle.

findings.summary: Refusal and closure objects were parsed as loose JSON values, so a refusal with a result or duplicate keys could settle.
findings.resolution: Refusals and closures deserialize into typed records with deny_unknown_fields; duplicate keys are refused; revision_refusal is admitted exactly for the agent-revision reasons; a closure must also match the request's admitted_envelope and carry result:null, accepted:false and integrated:false.

other_decisions: The credential environment is resolved right after claim authorization, before plan reservation, request sealing, admission, the transport binding and the transport intent (worker::credential_ordering_tests::a_refused_credential_is_rejected_before_any_plan_reservation asserts no reservation).
v2-only is enforced by config/implementation-worker.ncl and campaign binding; the direct worker runtime keeps its pre-existing v1 branch (transport_profile_mode_matches).

final_review.source: final re-review of cd9014a8; decisions by Main

finding.summary: prepare_launch_files persisted a transport binding at profile.output_directory before the owner-grant gate. A profile (or a competing process) whose gate then refused left a credible binding with no transport intent; after another profile launched in another root, a retry under the first profile recovered in its never-launched root, Lattice closed that empty root, and Kiln settled no execution while the real launch might still run.
finding.resolution: The binding file is removed as authority. kiln-core's AttemptLedger records a TransportLaunch {lattice_program, executable_blake3, state_directory} in dispatch_launches (serde default, skipped when empty) in the same mutation as the transport intent: begin_dispatch_transport(identity, fence, now_ms, plan, launch: Option<&TransportLaunch>) -> TransportStart returns Fresh, or Recover(recorded) with the recorded launch (None for an intent persisted before launches were recorded) and never overwrites it. settle_dispatch_without_execution, the only path that removes an intent, removes the launch too. Implementer::begin_dispatch_transport passes the launch through in the same transaction, and Implementer::dispatch_launch reads it. worker::run records the profile's launch only by winning the intent; recovery uses only the returned recorded launch and refuses without invoking Lattice when it is None, its root is not a real directory, or its program's BLAKE3 differs (worker_binding::recovery_launch, now a pure decision over the ledger launch). prepare_launch_files keeps the output directory, frozen request and first-launch state root before the gate, with no binding file. A closure settles only from a recovery that ran with the recorded launch. The workflow-exchange route in bin/lattice-dispatch.rs records no launch (None).
tests: kiln-core implementation::dispatch::tests::exact_worker_model_and_request_bindings_survive_reservation_and_reject_crossing (a recorded launch is returned to a later caller with another launch and never overwritten)

kiln-core implementation::dispatch::tests::legacy_intents_keep_their_encoding_and_never_gain_a_launch (old JSON without the field loads and an empty map is not serialized; a legacy intent recovers with None and never gains a launch; a recorded launch round-trips)
kiln-implementer tests/durable.rs before_effect_settlement_survives_restart_without_reconciliation (the launch survives restart with its intent and is cleared by settlement across restart)
kiln-adapter-lattice worker::preparation_tests::a_gate_refused_profile_never_directs_recovery (the reviewer's three steps: recovery under profile A gets B's recorded launch and A's root stays empty)
kiln-adapter-lattice worker::binding::tests::recovery_uses_only_the_recorded_launch and a_missing_or_symlinked_root_is_never_recovered (no launch, changed program, missing or symlinked root)
composed pregate-rejected, moved-root, lost-before-start, lost-during-run, refusals and crossed
finding.deviation: Reconciliation (reconcile_dispatch) keeps the transport intent so later calls recover, so it also keeps the launch; only settlement removes the intent and the launch, and the tests assert both.

final_review_2.source: final review of 8f036b29; decisions by Main

finding.summary: attempt.rs stored dispatch_launches inside the attempts document. Published Kiln binaries deserialize that document without the field and save the whole ledger back, even on reads through with_ledgers, so one operation by an older binary (for example an old web service beside a new CLI during a rolling upgrade) erases a recorded launch while leaving the intent; the next new dispatcher then gets Recover(None) and cannot recover in the intact recorded root.
finding.resolution: AttemptLedger and AttemptLedger::begin_dispatch_transport(identity, fence, now_ms, plan) -> CoreResult<bool> are restored to their published shape and semantics; the attempt.rs diff against 339116f6 is additive only. Launches live in a separate pure ledger, kiln_core::implementation::TransportLaunches { launches } (deny_unknown_fields), with start(identity, previously_started, launch) -> CoreResult<TransportStart> (records on a fresh intent, refuses a different existing record, recalls on an existing intent, None for legacy intents), recall(identity) and remove(identity). kiln-implementer stores it under the new kind TRANSPORT_LAUNCH_KIND = "transport_launches": begin_dispatch_transport(..., launch) and settle_dispatch_without_execution load attempts and transport_launches in one SQLite transaction (with_launches), apply both pure transitions and save both; every other path saves attempts only and leaves transport_launches untouched. A launch whose intent was cleared elsewhere is inert because recovery consults it only while the intent exists. Adapter call sites are unchanged.
tests: kiln-implementer tests/durable.rs an_older_attempt_writer_cannot_erase_a_recorded_launch (the attempts row is deserialized with the published AttemptLedger and re-saved byte-identically, an ordinary attempts-only save follows, and a new dispatcher under another profile still gets Recover(Some(recorded launch)))
kiln-core implementation::dispatch::tests::the_attempt_ledger_keeps_its_published_document_shape (the attempts JSON keys are exactly the 339116f6 fields)
kiln-core implementation::dispatch::tests::transport_launches_record_once_and_recall_only_for_an_existing_intent (record, recall, never overwrite, legacy None, remove, strict encoding)
kiln-implementer tests/durable.rs before_effect_settlement_survives_restart_without_reconciliation (the launch survives restart and is removed by settlement, both through the implementer)
